Air Capital paperwork: which Wichita NDT jobs certify under NAS 410 and which under SNT-TC-1A

In most Kansas towns an NDT technician never has to ask which personnel standard applies, because refinery, pipeline and fabrication work runs on written practices built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Wichita is the exception. Boeing completed its purchase of Spirit AeroSystems on December 8, 2025, and Spirit's commercial operations in the city, the 737 fuselage plant among them, are now Boeing. Textron Aviation builds Cessna and Beechcraft aircraft across several campuses, Bombardier keeps its US headquarters, flight test center and service center here, and a long tail of machining, forming, composite, heat-treat, plating and inspection houses ships parts to all of them. Where your employer sits in that chain decides whether your certification is written to NAS 410 or to SNT-TC-1A.

On the airframe supply chain

Aerostructures are bought on purchase orders, and the quality clauses on those orders are where the personnel standard gets named. Suppliers to airframe makers usually find NAS 410 there, or EN 4179 on European work, and the clause flows down to every sub-tier shop that inspects the hardware. In a NAS 410 shop a Responsible Level 3 (RL3), designated in writing, controls the written practice, the course outlines and the examinations, and Nadcap auditors working to AC7114 pull certification files and trace them back to training hours, experience logs and eye examinations. The big plants' own inspection departments certify under their own written practices, so ask the hiring Level 3 which standard and revision apply instead of guessing from the company name. The explainer on how NAS 410 certification works sets out the RL3's authority in detail.

Service centers, McConnell and the refinery belt

Maintenance NDT reaches its standard by a different road. A business-jet service center or a Part 145 repair station works to the personnel standard named in its own repair station manual and its customer contracts. The FAA does not certify NDT personnel, and its advisory circular AC 65-31B accepts several documents, NAS 410 and SNT-TC-1A among them. McConnell Air Force Base, home of the 22nd Air Refueling Wing and its KC-135 and KC-46 tankers, trains its uniformed NDI technicians under Air Force technical orders. Away from the airfields, the El Dorado refinery in Butler County, the crude and product pipelines that cross Kansas, and the city's HVAC, agricultural-equipment and trailer plants inspect to ASME, API and AWS codes, which call for SNT-TC-1A or CP-189. Plenty of Wichita technicians hold certifications under both systems over a career, one employer at a time.

Before you move from a plant job to an aerostructures supplier

  1. Ask the shop's RL3 which NAS 410 revision its written practice cites. Revision 6 was released in December 2025, and customers set the timing of the change.
  2. Expect to be certified again. Your SNT-TC-1A certificate is evidence the RL3 may credit, but it does not satisfy a NAS 410 requirement by itself.
  3. Plan for surface-method hours. NAS 410 expects more formal, documented penetrant and magnetic particle training than SNT-TC-1A recommends, and fluorescent penetrant is the daily method in many Wichita detail shops.
  4. Bring a complete file: course outlines with recorded hours, an experience log signed method by method, your examination history and a current vision record. Graduates of the WSU Tech program run with NIAR should keep their course records the same way, since a college awards coursework and only an employer awards certification.

For Wichita quality managers running both systems

Many shops in the Air Capital sell to an airframe customer and to an industrial one from the same floor. Keep two written practices, or one with clearly separated sections, and print the governing standard and revision on every certification letter so an auditor never has to guess. Keep training records to the NAS 410 level of evidence from day one, give everyone the stricter eye test where the two documents differ, and rehearse the walk from a signed inspection report back to the inspector's file before the Nadcap visit. Atlantis prepares and reviews that file set through NAS 410 audit documentation support for your RL3 to approve, and provides ASNT Level III consulting for Wichita aerospace suppliers, including written practices built on SNT-TC-1A and aligned to customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114.

Where Atlantis fits in Wichita

Atlantis training is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A: self-paced online theory with answers from our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), rehearsal in the Practical NDT aviation scenes, then the hands-on work and practical examination at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Wichita. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to any Wichita employer. If you work in a NAS 410 shop, the RL3 there decides whether outside coursework counts toward your certification, so get that answer before you enroll. For the side-by-side detail, read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A; for local aerospace methods, see aerospace NDT training in Wichita and penetrant testing training.
